title: Argumentative Texts
blurb: Claim, evidence and audience — three skills, then one full-topic proof.

core.title: Identify the Claim
core.skill: Finding the sentence the whole text is trying to make you agree with

activities.brief: Read the passage, then answer the questions.
sentences: Many schools should schedule outdoor learning days several times each year.
Learning outside can help students stay focused and engaged during lessons.
Science activities become more meaningful when students can observe plants, animals, and weather conditions firsthand.
Outdoor learning also encourages movement, which can improve attention and reduce stress.
Students often have opportunities to work together on hands-on projects while exploring their surroundings.
Some people worry that students may become distracted outside.
However, teachers can plan structured activities that keep students focused on learning.
For these reasons, schools should include outdoor learning days as part of the school year.
activities.hint: The claim is usually the first or last sentence, and it says what SHOULD happen.

questions.ask: Which sentence best states the author’s claim?
questions.answer: Many schools should schedule outdoor learning days several times each year.
options: Many schools should schedule outdoor learning days several times each year.
Some people worry that students may become distracted outside.
Outdoor learning also encourages movement, which can improve attention and reduce stress.

questions.ask: Which detail supports the claim?
questions.answer: Science activities become more meaningful when students can observe plants, animals, and weather conditions firsthand.
options: Science activities become more meaningful when students can observe plants, animals, and weather conditions firsthand.
Some people worry that students may become distracted outside.
Many schools should schedule outdoor learning days several times each year.

questions.ask: In your own words, what is the main claim the author makes?
questions.model: The author claims that schools should schedule outdoor learning days as part of the school year.

sentences: Communities should build more skate parks for children and teens.
Skate parks provide a safe place for people to practice skateboarding, roller skating, and other activities.
When riders have a designated area to use, they are less likely to skate in parking lots or busy streets.
Skate parks can also encourage exercise and help people spend more time outdoors.
Some residents worry that skate parks might create noise in nearby neighborhoods.
However, communities can choose locations that reduce disruptions while still giving young people a place to gather.
For these reasons, communities should invest in more skate parks.
activities.hint: An opposing claim is the one the author disagrees with.

questions.ask: Which sentence supports the author’s claim?
questions.answer: Skate parks provide a safe place for people to practice skateboarding, roller skating, and other activities.
options: Skate parks provide a safe place for people to practice skateboarding, roller skating, and other activities.
Some residents worry that skate parks might create noise in nearby neighborhoods.
Communities should build more skate parks for children and teens.

questions.ask: Which sentence presents an opposing claim?
questions.answer: Some residents worry that skate parks might create noise in nearby neighborhoods.
options: Some residents worry that skate parks might create noise in nearby neighborhoods.
Skate parks can also encourage exercise and help people spend more time outdoors.
For these reasons, communities should invest in more skate parks.

sentences: Students should learn basic cooking skills before they enter middle school.
Learning how to prepare simple meals can help children become more independent and responsible.
Cooking also teaches important skills such as following directions, measuring ingredients, and managing time.
Many children enjoy helping in the kitchen and trying new foods.
These experiences can build confidence and encourage healthy eating habits.
Basic cooking skills may also help families save money by preparing meals at home.
Some people believe cooking should only be taught by family members.
Even so, many adults agree that cooking is an important life skill that benefits children in many ways.
For these reasons, students should learn basic cooking skills at a young age.
activities.hint: Two sentences support the claim. One argues against it.

questions.ask: Which sentence supports the author’s claim?
questions.answer: Learning how to prepare simple meals can help children become more independent and responsible.
options: Learning how to prepare simple meals can help children become more independent and responsible.
Some people believe cooking should only be taught by family members.
Many children enjoy helping in the kitchen and trying new foods.

questions.ask: Which sentence presents an opposing claim?
questions.answer: Some people believe cooking should only be taught by family members.
options: Some people believe cooking should only be taught by family members.
Cooking also teaches important skills such as following directions, measuring ingredients, and managing time.
Basic cooking skills may also help families save money by preparing meals at home.

questions.ask: What is one claim the author makes in the selection?
questions.answer: Students should learn basic cooking skills before they enter middle school.
options: Learning how to prepare simple meals can help children become more independent and responsible.
Some people believe cooking should only be taught by family members.
Students should learn basic cooking skills before they enter middle school.
Basic cooking skills may also help families save money by preparing meals at home.

sentences: Free outdoor movie nights can be a valuable addition to community events.
Supporters argue that these events bring neighbors together in a fun and welcoming setting.
Families can enjoy entertainment without spending money on expensive tickets.
Outdoor movie nights also encourage residents to spend time in local parks and public spaces.
Some people think communities should spend money on other activities instead.
However, many residents believe movie nights help strengthen community connections while providing affordable entertainment.
activities.hint: Work backwards: what claim would this sentence be a reason FOR?

questions.ask: Which claim does this sentence support? “Families can enjoy entertainment without spending money on expensive tickets.”
questions.answer: Free outdoor movie nights can be a valuable addition to community events.
options: Free outdoor movie nights can be a valuable addition to community events.
Some people think communities should spend money on other activities instead.
Outdoor movie nights also encourage residents to spend time in local parks.

core.title: The Audience
core.skill: Working out who the author is actually talking to

activities.brief: Read the passage, then answer the questions.
sentences: Schools are considering adding more hands-on science activities to their classrooms.
Experiments and investigations allow students to apply concepts they learn from textbooks.
Research suggests that active participation can improve understanding and retention of information.
These activities also encourage collaboration and problem-solving skills.
Although additional materials may be required, the educational benefits can outweigh the costs.
School administrators should consider expanding opportunities for hands-on learning.
activities.hint: The last sentence usually names who is being asked to act.

questions.ask: Who is the author most likely addressing?
questions.model: The author is addressing school administrators, who are asked to expand hands-on learning.

questions.ask: Which reader would most likely agree with the author’s argument?
questions.answer: A principal looking for ways to improve instruction
options: A principal looking for ways to improve instruction
A scientist conducting research in a laboratory
A student studying for a college entrance exam

sentences: Many neighborhoods would benefit from establishing a community farmers market.
Farmers markets provide residents with access to fresh fruits, vegetables, and other locally produced goods.
Purchasing food from local growers can support small businesses and strengthen the local economy.
These markets also create opportunities for community members to gather and learn about healthy food choices.
Although organizing a market requires planning and coordination, the long-term benefits can positively affect many residents.
Community leaders should consider supporting this initiative.
activities.hint: Who is being asked to do something here?

questions.ask: Which detail would most interest the intended audience?
questions.answer: Purchasing food from local growers can support small businesses and strengthen the local economy.
options: Purchasing food from local growers can support small businesses and strengthen the local economy.
Organizing a market requires planning and coordination.
Farmers markets provide residents with fresh fruits and vegetables.

questions.ask: Who would most likely support this idea?
questions.model: Community leaders would most likely support it, because they are the ones asked to back the initiative.

sentences: Many families should consider adopting pets from local animal shelters.
Shelters care for animals that need safe and permanent homes.
Adopting a pet can provide companionship while also giving an animal a second chance.
Many shelters offer information about pet care and help families find animals that fit their lifestyles.
Although adopting a pet requires responsibility and commitment, the rewards can be meaningful for both families and animals.
People looking for a pet should visit their local shelter before purchasing one elsewhere.
activities.hint: Look at who the text keeps mentioning.

questions.ask: Who is most likely the intended audience of this passage?
questions.model: The intended audience is families who are thinking about getting a pet.

questions.ask: Which reader would most likely agree with the author’s argument?
questions.answer: A family deciding whether to adopt a pet
options: A family deciding whether to adopt a pet
A veterinarian performing surgery on animals
A scientist studying animal behavior
A zookeeper caring for exotic animals

questions.ask: Which detail would most interest the intended audience?
questions.answer: Many shelters offer information about pet care and help families find animals that fit their lifestyles.
options: Shelters provide safe homes for animals while they await adoption.
Many shelters offer information about pet care and help families find animals that fit their lifestyles.
Adopting a pet requires time, effort, and daily responsibility.
Pets often provide companionship and comfort for their owners.

sentences: More students should join school chess clubs.
Playing chess requires strategic thinking and careful decision-making.
Students who participate often strengthen their problem-solving abilities while learning from both victories and mistakes.
Students should consider joining a chess club if one is available.
activities.hint: Short text, but it says who it is for twice.

questions.ask: Who is most likely the intended audience of this text?
questions.model: The intended audience is students who might join a school chess club.

core.title: For or Against an Argument
core.skill: Spotting the facts an author uses, and what each one is doing

activities.brief: Read the passage, then answer the questions.
sentences: Community centers should offer more esports tournaments for students.
Esports are video game competitions where players work together as a team.
These games help students practice teamwork and quick thinking.
According to a survey by several youth programs, more students joined community activities after esports events were added.
Some people believe community centers should focus only on traditional sports.
However, many organizers say esports give students another fun way to stay active and involved.
For these reasons, community centers should offer more esports tournaments.
activities.hint: A fact usually says where it came from — a survey, a study, records.

questions.ask: Which sentence uses a fact to support the claim about esports?
questions.answer: According to a survey by several youth programs, more students joined community activities after esports events were added.
options: According to a survey by several youth programs, more students joined community activities after esports events were added.
Esports are video game competitions where players work together as a team.
Some people believe community centers should focus only on traditional sports.

questions.ask: “Some people believe community centers should focus only on traditional sports.” How does the author argue against this idea?
questions.model: The author answers it by saying many organizers think esports give students another fun way to stay active and involved.

sentences: Public libraries should offer more hands-on workshops for children.
In these workshops, kids can learn skills like coding, building, and art.
Library attendance records from several cities show that more people visit when workshops are offered often.
Workshops also help children discover new interests and solve problems in creative ways.
Some people believe libraries should focus only on books and reading.
However, many communities have found that workshops bring in more visitors while helping kids learn outside the classroom.
For these reasons, libraries should offer more workshops for children.
activities.hint: Attendance records are evidence. Ask what they are evidence OF.

questions.ask: Which sentence provides factual evidence that workshops benefit libraries?
questions.answer: Library attendance records from several cities show that more people visit when workshops are offered often.
options: Library attendance records from several cities show that more people visit when workshops are offered often.
In these workshops, kids can learn skills like coding, building, and art.
Some people believe libraries should focus only on books and reading.

questions.ask: Why did the author include the information about attendance records?
questions.answer: To provide evidence that workshops attract more visitors
options: To explain how libraries organize books
To provide evidence that workshops attract more visitors
To show that workshops are difficult to plan
To compare libraries in different cities

sentences: Many communities should build more bike trails for residents.
Bike trails provide safe places for people to ride away from busy roads and traffic.
According to transportation studies, communities with dedicated bike paths often report fewer bicycle-related accidents than areas without them.
Bike trails also encourage people to spend more time exercising outdoors.
Some people believe communities should spend money on different projects instead.
However, many residents argue that safer routes and healthier lifestyles make bike trails a worthwhile investment.
activities.hint: One sentence raises the objection. The next one answers it.

questions.ask: Which sentence uses a fact to support the argument that bike trails improve safety?
questions.answer: According to transportation studies, communities with dedicated bike paths often report fewer bicycle-related accidents than areas without them.
options: According to transportation studies, communities with dedicated bike paths often report fewer bicycle-related accidents than areas without them.
Bike trails provide safe places for people to ride away from busy roads and traffic.
Bike trails also encourage people to spend more time exercising outdoors.

questions.ask: Which sentence argues against the idea that communities should spend money on different projects instead?
questions.answer: However, many residents argue that safer routes and healthier lifestyles make bike trails a worthwhile investment.
options: However, many residents argue that safer routes and healthier lifestyles make bike trails a worthwhile investment.
Some people believe communities should spend money on different projects instead.
Many communities should build more bike trails for residents.

questions.ask: How does the fact about transportation studies support the author’s argument?
questions.answer: It provides evidence that bike trails can reduce accidents and make riding safer.
options: It describes why some people disagree with building bike trails.
It shows that all residents use bike trails every day.
It explains how communities build bike trails.
It provides evidence that bike trails can reduce accidents and make riding safer.

sentences: Communities should install more free water bottle refill stations in public parks.
These stations make it easier for visitors to stay hydrated while spending time outdoors.
Refill stations can also reduce the use of single-use plastic bottles, which helps decrease waste.
In addition, families can save money by refilling reusable bottles instead of purchasing drinks.
Some people think installing refill stations would cost too much money.
However, many residents believe the benefits to health and the environment make refill stations a worthwhile investment.
activities.hint: Ask what reason this sentence gives for agreeing with the claim.

questions.ask: How does this sentence support the author’s argument? “Refill stations can also reduce the use of single-use plastic bottles, which helps decrease waste.”
questions.model: It gives a reason to install the stations by showing they cut down on single-use plastic and reduce waste.

arg_claim.title: SB: Identify the Claim
arg_claim.skill: Claim, reason, opposing view — one passage at a time

activities.brief: In each passage, which sentence is the author’s claim?
activities.hint: A claim says what SHOULD happen. An opposing view starts with “Some people…”.

items.given: Schools should start the day a little later in the morning. Many students do not get enough sleep on school nights… Some people believe an early start helps families keep a steady routine.  →  ____
items.answer: Schools should start the day a little later in the morning.
options: Schools should start the day a little later in the morning.
Many students do not get enough sleep on school nights.
Some people believe an early start helps families keep a steady routine.

items.given: Students should learn to type on a keyboard in elementary school. Typing helps kids finish their schoolwork faster… Some people think students should focus only on handwriting.  →  ____
items.answer: Students should learn to type on a keyboard in elementary school.
options: Students should learn to type on a keyboard in elementary school.
Typing helps kids finish their schoolwork faster and with fewer mistakes.
Some people think students should focus only on handwriting.

sentences: Children should help with chores around the house.
Doing chores teaches kids how to be responsible and care for their home.
It also helps them learn skills they will use as adults.
Many families find that sharing chores makes the work easier for everyone.
Some people believe children are too busy with school to help at home.
Still, many parents agree that chores teach lessons that last a lifetime.
activities.hint: The claim is the opinion. The rest are reasons for it.

questions.ask: What is the main claim the author makes in the passage?
questions.answer: Children should help with chores around the house.
options: Doing chores teaches kids how to be responsible and care for their home.
Children should help with chores around the house.
Some people believe children are too busy with school to help at home.

sentences: Neighborhoods should build more public pickleball courts for families and residents.
Pickleball is a fast-growing sport that people of many ages can enjoy together.
Public courts provide a place for exercise, recreation, and community events.
Families can spend time outdoors while staying active and meeting new people.
The courts may also encourage residents to participate in healthy activities more often.
Some people think parks should use their space for other activities instead.
However, many residents believe pickleball courts give communities another way to stay active and connect with neighbors.
activities.hint: One of these three is the claim and one is the opposing claim.

questions.ask: What is the main claim the author makes in the passage?
questions.answer: Neighborhoods should build more public pickleball courts for families and residents.
options: Neighborhoods should build more public pickleball courts for families and residents.
Public courts provide a place for exercise, recreation, and community events.
Some people think parks should use their space for other activities instead.

questions.ask: Which sentence best states the opposing claim?
questions.answer: Some people think parks should use their space for other activities instead.
options: Neighborhoods should build more public pickleball courts for families and residents.
Public courts provide a place for exercise, recreation, and community events.
Some people think parks should use their space for other activities instead.

sentences: Students should keep a daily journal at school.
Writing each day helps students improve their spelling and grammar.
A journal also gives students a private place to share their ideas and feelings.
Over time, students can look back and see how their writing has grown.
Some people believe journaling takes time away from other lessons.
However, many teachers find that daily writing makes students stronger and more confident.
activities.hint: A reason answers "why should we?"

questions.ask: Which sentence is a reason the author gives to support the claim?
questions.answer: Writing each day helps students improve their spelling and grammar.
options: Writing each day helps students improve their spelling and grammar.
Some people believe journaling takes time away from other lessons.
Students should keep a daily journal at school.

arg_audience.title: SB: The Audience
arg_audience.skill: Reading the clues that say who an argument is for

activities.brief: Each argument is written for one group. Which one?
activities.hint: Look at what the writer wants built. One group in the bank is never used.

items.given: Our winged beasts deserve new landing pads and roomy stables, because they need a safe place to rest their wings between long flights.  →  ____
A grand stage with bright enchanted lanterns is worth fighting for, because your songs and tales deserve a place to be heard by cheering crowds.  →  ____
Training matters, so insist on a practice yard with dummies and shields, because you must sharpen your sword and shield before the next great battle.  →  ____
Mastering powerful magic requires a tower library of ancient scrolls, because spells cannot be learned without a quiet place to study them in peace.  →  ____
Healing the whole kingdom starts with a cauldron room of rare herbs, because brewing strong potions all year long demands the right space and ingredients.  →  ____

activities.brief: Read the passage, then answer the questions.
sentences: Students should be allowed to create a class pet rock museum.
Each student could decorate a rock, give it a funny name, and write a short description about its “personality.”
The museum would give students a creative way to practice writing and speaking.
It could also help classmates learn more about one another through humor and imagination.
Some people may think pet rocks are silly, but fun projects can still build useful classroom skills.
Teachers should consider adding a pet rock museum as a creative class activity.
activities.hint: A different audience needs a different reason. Ask what each group cares about.

questions.ask: Who is most likely the intended audience of this text?
questions.model: The audience is teachers, because the last sentence asks them to add the museum.

questions.ask: What detail might they include to be more convincing for parents?
questions.answer: The project could help students practice writing and speaking skills.
options: Some pet rocks might be painted with bright colors and patterns.
Students could give their pet rocks funny names and personalities.
The project could help students practice writing and speaking skills.

questions.ask: What detail might they include to be more convincing for students?
questions.answer: Students could vote for the funniest pet rock in the museum.
options: Students could vote for the funniest pet rock in the museum.
Teachers could use the project to practice writing skills.
The museum could be displayed near the classroom door.

sentences: Students should join a lunchroom comedy club if one is offered at school.
Telling jokes and writing short skits can help students become more confident speakers.
Club members would learn how to organize ideas, use appropriate humor, and perform for an audience.
The club could also give students a fun way to make friends during the school year.
Although performing can feel nervous at first, practice can make it easier.
Students who enjoy making others laugh should consider joining the club.
activities.hint: Who does the text keep saying "you" to?

questions.ask: Who is the intended audience of the passage above?
questions.model: The audience is students, especially ones who enjoy making other people laugh.

arg_facts.title: SB: Facts For an Argument
arg_facts.skill: Which facts help an argument, and which just sit there

activities.brief: Read the passage, then answer the questions.
sentences: Schools should give students the chance to plant and care for their own gardens.
Working in a garden teaches young people responsibility, because seeds must be watered and weeded regularly in order to grow.
Studies have found that students who help grow vegetables are more willing to taste healthy foods they once avoided.
Gardening also lets children spend time outdoors instead of staring at screens all afternoon.
Gardens look most colorful when the flowers bloom in late spring.
By caring for living plants, students learn patience and discover how their own effort can produce something valuable.
activities.hint: One sentence is true but does nothing for the argument.

questions.ask: Which sentence does NOT support the claim that gardening helps students?
questions.answer: Gardens look most colorful when the flowers bloom in late spring.
options: Gardens look most colorful when the flowers bloom in late spring.
Working in a garden teaches young people responsibility.
Gardening also lets children spend time outdoors instead of staring at screens.

questions.ask: Which sentence would be a strong replacement?
questions.answer: Caring for a garden can teach students how plants change with the seasons.
options: Some students prefer to eat lunch outside with their friends.
Caring for a garden can teach students how plants change with the seasons.
Many gardens are surrounded by tall wooden fences.

questions.ask: Which fact best supports the author’s claim that gardening helps students?
questions.answer: Growing vegetables can encourage students to eat healthier foods.
options: Growing vegetables can encourage students to eat healthier foods.
Gardens often attract bees and colorful butterflies in the spring.
Many families grow flowers in their backyards at home.

sentences: Communities should plant more trees along their neighborhood streets.
Tall trees provide cooling shade that lowers temperatures on hot summer days, which helps people stay comfortable outdoors.
Their leaves also clean the air by absorbing harmful gases and releasing fresh oxygen for everyone to breathe.
Trees give birds and squirrels safe places to build nests and search for food.
Some people think planting trees costs too much money.
But cities save far more over time because shade trees lower cooling bills and reduce costly road repairs.
In addition, neighborhoods filled with trees often look more peaceful and welcoming to the families who live there.
activities.hint: An author raises an objection on purpose, then knocks it down.

questions.ask: Which sentence is the opposing fact?
questions.answer: Some people think planting trees costs too much money.
options: Some people think planting trees costs too much money.
Tall trees provide cooling shade that lowers temperatures on hot summer days.
Trees give birds and squirrels safe places to build nests.

questions.ask: Which sentence disproves it?
questions.answer: But cities save far more over time because shade trees lower cooling bills and reduce costly road repairs.
options: But cities save far more over time because shade trees lower cooling bills and reduce costly road repairs.
Their leaves also clean the air by absorbing harmful gases.
Communities should plant more trees along their neighborhood streets.

questions.ask: Why did the author include a fact that argues against planting trees?
questions.answer: To show the opposing idea is wrong and make the argument stronger.
options: To prove that trees really are too expensive to plant.
To show the opposing idea is wrong and make the argument stronger.
To change the subject to something new.

sentences: Schools should set aside time each day for students to read books they choose themselves.
Reading for enjoyment helps students build larger vocabularies and become stronger, more confident readers.
When children pick their own books, they are far more likely to stay interested and finish the story.
Quiet reading time also gives busy students a calm break during a long school day.
Recess usually lasts about twenty minutes.
Because reading widens the imagination and strengthens the mind, daily reading time is a valuable use of the school schedule.
activities.hint: Ask what the sentence proves about the claim.

questions.ask: How did including this sentence support the author’s argument? “Reading for enjoyment helps students build larger vocabularies and become stronger, more confident readers.”
questions.answer: It supports the claim by giving a reason that free reading improves students’ skills.
options: It explains that students should only read during recess.
It supports the claim by giving a reason that free reading improves students’ skills.
It describes how teachers choose books for the class library.

full.title: Full Topic: Argumentative Texts
full.skill: Claim, evidence and audience, in one piece of writing

activities.brief: Read the passage, then answer the questions.
sentences: Every student knows the worst part of lunch: staring at a warm, gooey brownie while choking down a pile of cold, rubbery green beans.
For this reason, our cafeteria should serve dessert before the main meal.
Eating dessert first would actually improve our health, because hungry students would still have plenty of room left for vegetables afterward.
Scientists have never officially proven that brownies cause harm, which practically means they are good for you.
Some adults claim that sugar makes children wild and impossible to control.
However, anyone who has watched a fifth grader after gym class knows that we were already wild to begin with.
A happy stomach leads to a happy brain, so the cafeteria should flip the menu and let dessert lead the way.
activities.hint: One of these reasons proves nothing at all, even though it sounds scientific.

questions.ask: Which sentence best states the author’s claim?
questions.answer: For this reason, our cafeteria should serve dessert before the main meal.
options: For this reason, our cafeteria should serve dessert before the main meal.
Some adults claim that sugar makes children wild and impossible to control.
Every student knows the worst part of lunch.

questions.ask: Which sentence gives the weakest support for the claim?
questions.answer: Scientists have never officially proven that brownies cause harm, which practically means they are good for you.
options: Scientists have never officially proven that brownies cause harm, which practically means they are good for you.
Eating dessert first would actually improve our health, because hungry students would still have room for vegetables.
A happy stomach leads to a happy brain.

sentences: Parents, it is time to face an uncomfortable truth.
Children deserve to be paid for doing their chores.
Cleaning a messy bedroom is exhausting work, and no skilled worker should be expected to fold laundry for free.
Paying us for chores would also teach valuable money skills, since we would quickly learn to spend our earnings on candy and video games.
Hard workers always do their best when a reward is waiting, and nothing rewards a kid like cold, hard cash.
Of course, some parents argue that helping around the house is simply part of being in a family.
That may sound lovely on a greeting card, but a family is really a tiny business, and every business pays its workers.
A small weekly allowance would transform grumpy chore-doers into eager helpers almost overnight.
For the good of the entire household, parents should start handing out paychecks today.
activities.hint: The very first word tells you who this is written for.

questions.ask: Which sentence is the author’s claim?
questions.answer: Children deserve to be paid for doing their chores.
options: Children deserve to be paid for doing their chores.
Cleaning a messy bedroom is exhausting work.
Some parents argue that helping around the house is part of being in a family.

questions.ask: Which sentence gives a reason against the author’s claim?
questions.answer: Of course, some parents argue that helping around the house is simply part of being in a family.
options: Of course, some parents argue that helping around the house is simply part of being in a family.
A small weekly allowance would transform grumpy chore-doers into eager helpers.
Hard workers always do their best when a reward is waiting.

questions.ask: Who is the intended audience of this passage?
questions.model: The intended audience is parents, because the passage speaks to them directly from the first word.

sentences: Students should be allowed to take a short nap during the school day.
Well-rested kids learn better and concentrate longer.
By lunchtime, many fifth graders are completely exhausted, yawning through math and daydreaming about their cozy pillows at home.
A quick afternoon nap could recharge their tired brains and help them remember much more of each lesson.
Some students enjoy collecting trading cards during recess.
Of course, some teachers worry that a daily nap would waste valuable learning minutes.
Still, supporters believe that a rested, focused student accomplishes far more in the end.
activities.hint: One sentence in here is about something else entirely.

questions.ask: Which detail does NOT support the author’s claim?
questions.answer: Some students enjoy collecting trading cards during recess.
options: Some students enjoy collecting trading cards during recess.
Well-rested kids learn better and concentrate longer.
A quick afternoon nap could recharge their tired brains.

sentences: Recess should be much longer, because fresh air and free time help students focus better once they return to class.
Running, climbing, and laughing give kids a chance to burn off extra energy that would otherwise turn into wiggling and whispering.
Longer recess could improve health, lift students’ moods, and even strengthen friendships across different grades.
Studies suggest that active bodies lead to sharper minds, so a longer break might actually raise test scores.
For all of these reasons, many students believe a longer recess would make the entire school day better.
activities.hint: Claim, audience, and one piece of evidence.

questions.ask: Finish the sentence: the author’s claim is…
questions.model: that recess should be much longer, because it helps students focus when they return to class.

questions.ask: Finish the sentence: the intended audience is…
questions.model: students, and the school leaders who decide how long recess lasts.

questions.ask: How does this sentence support the author’s claim? “Studies suggest that active bodies lead to sharper minds, so a longer break might actually raise test scores.”
questions.model: It gives evidence from studies that being active sharpens the mind, which suggests a longer recess could raise test scores.
